concepts.title: HTTP caching
concepts.brief: Compare browser caching, CDN caching, and application caching.
tasks: Explain Cache-Control, ETag, and conditional requests.
Trace a request before and after a cached response expires.
Show how to avoid caching private user data.

concepts.title: Database indexes
concepts.brief: Investigate how an index changes database reads and writes.
tasks: Create a PostgreSQL table and compare EXPLAIN plans with and without an index.
Explain composite index column order with an example.
Describe storage and write overhead.

concepts.title: Idempotency
concepts.brief: Learn how to safely handle a request that arrives more than once.
tasks: Explain idempotency using a payment request.
Sketch an idempotency-key table and concurrent request handling.
Discuss expiration and retries after a timeout.

concepts.title: Queues and delivery guarantees
concepts.brief: Explore asynchronous processing and duplicate delivery.
tasks: Compare at-most-once and at-least-once delivery.
Implement or sketch an idempotent consumer.
Explain retry backoff and dead-letter queues.

concepts.title: Transactions and isolation
concepts.brief: Explore concurrent updates to shared data.
tasks: Demonstrate a lost update with two transactions.
Compare isolation levels and row locking.
Explain when a transaction cannot cover an external API call.

concepts.title: OAuth and OpenID Connect
concepts.brief: Understand delegated access and user sign-in.
tasks: Draw an authorization-code flow with PKCE.
Explain access tokens, ID tokens, and refresh tokens.
Identify where token validation and secure storage happen.

concepts.title: Observability
concepts.brief: Understand logs, metrics, and traces in a distributed request.
tasks: Trace an HTTP request through an API and database.
Choose useful latency, error, and saturation metrics.
Explain correlation IDs and secret redaction.

concepts.title: Load balancing and health checks
concepts.brief: Explore routing traffic across application instances.
tasks: Compare layer 4 and layer 7 balancing.
Distinguish readiness, liveness, and startup checks.
Explain connection draining during deployment.

concepts.title: Consistency and replication
concepts.brief: Explore the behavior of replicated data.
tasks: Explain a stale read after a successful write.
Compare strong and eventual consistency for a shopping cart.
Describe read-your-writes behavior and its cost.

concepts.title: Timeouts and circuit breakers
concepts.brief: Learn how services limit the impact of dependency failures.
tasks: Choose a timeout budget for a chain of API calls.
Explain exponential backoff with jitter.
Sketch circuit breaker states and recovery.

concepts.title: Infrastructure as code state
concepts.brief: Explore how Terraform maps configuration to cloud resources.
tasks: Explain configuration, state, and real infrastructure.
Describe state locking and drift detection.
Outline secure remote state storage and recovery.

concepts.title: Network boundaries
concepts.brief: Explore private subnets and application connectivity.
tasks: Trace traffic from a public load balancer to a private API and database.
Explain routes, security groups, and NAT.
Describe how a VPC-connected Lambda reaches a private database.

systemDesign.title: Stripe payment inside a transaction
systemDesign.brief: Your checkout opens a database transaction, creates an order, calls Stripe, then commits. Stripe sometimes times out; other times payment succeeds but the database commit fails.
tasks: Identify what a database rollback cannot undo.
Sketch a safer order/payment flow, including an unknown payment outcome.
Explain how a retry avoids charging twice.

systemDesign.title: Email failure breaks signup
systemDesign.brief: Signup creates a user and then sends a welcome email. When the email provider fails, the API returns an error even though the user already exists.
tasks: Decide when signup should count as successful.
Sketch a small change that lets the email be retried.
Explain how you avoid sending the same welcome email twice.

systemDesign.title: Duplicate webhook updates
systemDesign.brief: A payment webhook is delivered twice and your handler adds account credit twice.
tasks: Identify why checking the balance first is insufficient.
Sketch how to record and apply each event only once, even concurrently.
Describe one test for duplicate delivery.

systemDesign.title: Two people book the same slot
systemDesign.brief: Your API checks whether a slot is free, then inserts a booking. Two simultaneous requests both succeed.
tasks: Explain the race between the check and insert.
Propose one database change that prevents double booking.
Decide what response the losing request receives.

systemDesign.title: Stale cache after an edit
systemDesign.brief: Updating a product saves the new price to the database, but the next page load still shows the cached old price.
tasks: Locate the stale-data path.
Choose a small cache update or invalidation strategy.
Explain what happens if that cache operation fails.

systemDesign.title: Worker crashes after sending
systemDesign.brief: A worker sends a notification, then crashes before acknowledging its queue message. The job is delivered again.
tasks: Explain why the second delivery occurs.
Sketch how to prevent or reduce duplicate sends, including provider limitations.
Describe when the message should be acknowledged.

systemDesign.title: A slow API holds the request open
systemDesign.brief: Your endpoint calls a shipping provider that sometimes takes 40 seconds. Requests pile up while waiting.
tasks: Choose a timeout and a useful response to the user.
Sketch how the user can retry or check progress.
Explain one risk of automatically retrying the provider call.

systemDesign.title: Upload leaves an orphaned file
systemDesign.brief: A file upload to object storage succeeds, but saving its database record fails. The file is left behind.
tasks: Sketch a small upload status flow.
Choose how to detect and clean up orphaned files.
Explain what a retry should reuse or replace.

systemDesign.title: Double-click creates two orders
systemDesign.brief: A customer double-clicks Pay and the server receives two identical checkout requests.
tasks: Explain why disabling the button alone is insufficient.
Sketch server-side deduplication for concurrent requests.
Decide what the second request should return.

systemDesign.title: One failed item restarts a batch
systemDesign.brief: A scheduled job processes 100 invoices. Invoice 73 fails, and rerunning the job processes the first 72 again.
tasks: Choose a way to track progress per invoice.
Sketch retry behavior for the failed invoice.
Explain how already completed invoices avoid duplicate side effects.

systemDesign.title: Lost profile updates
systemDesign.brief: Two browser tabs read the same profile. One changes the phone number, the other saves an old copy and overwrites that change.
tasks: Explain the lost update.
Choose partial updates or version checks and show a tiny request example.
Describe how the client handles a conflict.

systemDesign.title: Webhook arrives before the response
systemDesign.brief: A payment-success webhook reaches your server before the checkout request has saved the provider payment ID. The handler cannot find the order.
tasks: Sketch how to link the order and payment before making the external call.
Explain how to handle an event whose order is not found yet.
Describe how the late checkout response avoids overwriting a successful status.
